added_models.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)

engagement.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)
engagement.population: ER-positive luminal B and triple-negative breast cancer, presurgical single dose of dalotuzumab 20 mg/kg
engagement.confidence_note: Registry record only (first posted 2008-09-25). The 101-gene GFS is Merck's growth-factor-pathway signature (US patent 8392127, Watters/Loboda/Nebozhyn: found in AKT-inhibitor-phenotyped colon lines, checked against growth-factor-stimulated MCF7/HT29 and MK-0646 xenograft growth inhibition); a patent is not an admissible tier, so the model side rests on the registry. It is not the Creighton 2008 MCF-7 IGF-I signature.
engagement.note: Merck's 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature, scored on paired tumour biopsies, set as the proof-of-biology endpoint: dalotuzumab should lower it in at least 40% of patients.
engagement.quote: The primary hypothesis is that dalotuzumab will induce a decrease in the GFS in at least 40% of participants.
engagement.judgement: A separate system from the MCF-7 xenograft tracks: an in-silico transcriptional classifier applied to patient biopsies, carrying its own prediction (signature reversal in at least 40% of dosed tumours).

engagement.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)
engagement.population: ER-positive luminal B and triple-negative breast cancer, presurgical single dose of dalotuzumab 20 mg/kg
engagement.confidence_note: Registry results only (posted 2017-04-14; results first submitted 2016-11-21; no peer-reviewed report found). Values are percentages with 80% CI (as posted); the ER+ interval (13.1-49.2) spans 40% even at that width, so the miss is at point-estimate level, and a reader applying 'partial' would score same. The direct secondary readout, IGF1R membrane H-score, fell by a median 104.5 in ER+ and 11.5 in TN (n=13 each), so the receptor was hit while the signature mostly did not move. The model side is the same registry record (the signature's derivation is only in a patent).
engagement.note: A single 20 mg/kg dose lowered the GFS in 28.6% of ER+ and 17.6% of TN tumours, below the prespecified 40% proof-of-biology bar in both cohorts.
engagement.short: GFS fell in fewer than 40% predicted
engagement.quote: Percentage of Participants Demonstrating a Decrease in the Growth Factor Signature (GFS): ER-positive Luminal B 28.6 (13.1 to 49.2); Triple Negative 17.6 (6.7 to 35.2) percentage of participants.
engagement.judgement: The prespecified proof-of-biology hypothesis failed in both cohorts on point estimates: the signature moved in a minority while the direct readout (IGF1R H-score) fell, so the in-silico readout, not target engagement, missed. Scored contra rather than same+partial because the trial's own bar was the prediction; the registry makes no call, so comparison_stated is false.
engagement.reason: Signature fell in fewer than 40% predicted

efficacy.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)
efficacy.population: ER-positive luminal B and triple-negative breast cancer, presurgical single dose of dalotuzumab 20 mg/kg
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record only. The patent claims the GFS classifies growth-factor-deregulated tumours and predicts response, but no breast trial of a member antibody stratified or analysed outcome by GFS: NCT00759785 correlated GFS response only with IGF1R IHC, and NCT01220570 (GFS as an intermediate biomarker of response; ridaforolimus, dalotuzumab or both; 63 patients, completed 2012-12) never posted results.
efficacy.note: Signature claimed to classify growth-factor-deregulated tumours and predict response; never used to select patients for a member antibody, and NCT01220570 posted no results.
efficacy.quote: A study to evaluate the response of growth factor signatures (GFS) to a single dose of dalotuzumab in participants with triple negative (TN) or estrogen receptor (ER)-positive luminal B breast cancer.
efficacy.judgement: The response-prediction claim is a patient-level efficacy prediction, but the only comparisons made were pharmacodynamic (engagement), so efficacy stays untested on this track.

considered_not_added: Ganitumab in breast cancer (Robertson 2013 Lancet Oncol, doi 10.1016/S1470-2045(13)70026-3; I-SPY 2 ganitumab+metformin, Yee 2021 npj Breast Cancer, doi 10.1038/s41523-021-00337-2): same mechanism but not a member of this tile; not widened, its patient data score nowhere here.

Di Cosimo 2015 model identity (only in-vivo system is the NSCLC-derived xenograft LXFA629; breast prediction rests on MCF7 in vitro): a re-keying of the existing track ridaforolimus-dalotuzumab-pathway-models, not a missing system.

Creighton 2008 MCF-7 IGF-I gene signature (doi 10.1200/JCO.2007.13.4429) and its model-side reversal by anti-IGF-IR antibodies in Litzenburger 2011 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-10-1903): the checker's lead keyed NCT00759785's endpoint to it, but the trial's 101-gene GFS is Merck's patented growth-factor-pathway signature (US 8392127), a different model program; the academic signature was never compared with patients dosed with a member antibody (Litzenburger's full text names no member; its tumorgraft arm used the TKI BMS-754807, outside the class), so it has no track.

Veligrotug cynomolgus repeat-dose toxicology (FDA PharmR 761530, General Toxicity: 'there was no effect on hearing capacity in the 27-week toxicity study in monkeys', NOAEL 50 mg/kg/week, vs label 5.3 Hyperglycemia and 5.4 Hearing Impairment Including Hearing Loss, approval 2026): the same system as the draft's cyno-toxicology-teprotumumab track (same model, same silent prediction, same harms), so it belongs as a strengthening contra entry on that track, not a new one.

NCT01220570 (GFS as an intermediate biomarker of response; ridaforolimus, dalotuzumab or both in ER+/HER2- breast cancer; 63 patients; completed 2012-12): same GFS system, but no results were posted and no publication was found, so nothing to score; noted on the added track.
Laron syndrome / GHR-deficiency human genetic model: searches returned only reviews; no source compares it with member-antibody trial results in breast cancer.
Patient-derived xenografts, organoids, ex-vivo explants and PK/PD or QSP dose models for cixutumumab or dalotuzumab in breast cancer: no paper with a patient comparison found in Europe PMC.
